symptom: A second Sonatype Lifecycle scan, run after the v2.9.2 upgrade (ako/mxcli#1372), still blocked the release: github.com/klauspost/compress v1.19.2 Critical:1, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver v1.17.10 Critical:1, and github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb v1.10.0. mongo-driver/v2 v2.9.2 had cleared and was gone from the report
cause: Three unrelated causes behind one report. (1) klauspost/compress v1.19.2 predates GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8 (zstd DecodeAll crash on crafted input), fixed in v1.20.2 — the previous PR had only raised it to whatever mongo-driver/v2@v2.9.2 declared, which was not a security floor. (2) The v1 mongo-driver line has NO fix for CVE-2026-107325 and never will: v1.17.10 is the last v1 release and the module is marked deprecated. (3) go-mssqldb v1.10.0 was simply behind v1.11.2
file: `go.mod` — klauspost/compress v1.19.2 -> v1.20.3 (explicit indirect), go-mssqldb v1.10.0 -> v1.11.2; `sql/drivers_test.go` (new)
insight: Measure the vulnerable SYMBOL in the exact version, do not reason from the module's advisory range — v1 and v2 of mongo-driver are separate implementations and behave differently on the same payload. Measured on v1.17.10: `bsoncore.Array.Validate([]byte{0,0,0,0})` panics with `index out of range [-1]` (CVE-2026-107325, unfixed and unfixable on v1), while `bson.Raw.Validate` on the CVE-2026-107324 MaxInt32 payload does NOT panic — that CVE's code path is v2-only, so the v1 report overstates by one. Identical result on v1.17.9, proving the v1.17.10 bump bought nothing for these two and was only CVE-2026-88031 (GridFS). mxcli is not exposed: every `.Validate()` call site in the tree imports v2 (checked by pairing each call site against its file's imports), mxcli imports v1 `x/bsonx/bsoncore` in ZERO files, and `bson.Unmarshal` — the v1 API it actually uses, 112 times on .mpr bytes — does not panic on any malformed payload tried. So the v1 finding is real in the module and unreachable in this program, and no upgrade can ever clear it; only dropping the v1 dependency (107 non-test + 179 test files) can. Second trap, same shape as the first scan's: klauspost/compress still has NO go.sum entry and no `go version -m` line at v1.20.3 — never compiled — yet raising the declared requirement is what clears a graph-reading scanner, so the one-line bump is worth it even though no code changes. A blank-import driver registration (`sql/drivers.go`) had no test at all, so a bump could drop a driver name and only fail at connect time in front of a user: `TestExternalDriversRegistered` now covers it, and fails with `driver "sqlserver" is not registered` when the import is removed
